subject: Request: trace-playback for high-cost chat flows
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: trace-playback for high-cost chat flows

Team — quick summary from this morning's call with Acme (Sara + Oliver): they're seeing a small number of chat flows that account for ~40% of their token spend and occasional 95th percentile latency spikes. They sent over a file with examples (attached).

Big ask from their PM: a console feature that lets us (and them) replay a single request end-to-end in a safe, read-only sandbox and see a per-token cost/time breakdown + model variant & KV-cache state at each step. Concretely they'd like: 
- a compact "trace snippet" UI that surfaces prompt tokens, model selection, quantization variant, and token-level latency/cost;
- ability to expand into a replay that executes the request on an isolated sandbox instance (no customer data retained) to validate whether model variant / temperature / batching changed the outcome;
- links from traces to raw logs and the request's stored prompt/response;
- an easy way to pin a trace to a route slice to watch regressions over time.

Why this matters: Acme uses this to justify switching heavyweight flows to cheaper model variants and to debug when a minor prompt edit causes a big cost regression. For Redwood, it reduces support cycles and makes "why did cost jump" questions answerable in a single ticket.

Asks: 
1) Product: can we scope a minimal "trace snippet" (UI + server API + storage TTL) as a short-term ship (2 sprints)?
2) Infra/Runtime: what are our constraints for storing trace artifacts and for spinning a sandbox replay without affecting production fleet?
3) Legal/Security: ensure the sandbox replay has no persistence of PII and obeys tenant isolation rules — cc'ing Evelyn for constraints.

I've attached the sample CSV from Acme and a few example request IDs. Would like to propose we sync tomorrow to pick owners and next actions.

Attachments: sample-highcost-requests.csv (CSV, 12 rows)

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: trace-playback for high-cost chat flows

Thanks Mateo — digging into the ask, a few technical clarifications/questions before we commit scope: 

1) Data model: do we intend to store the full token stream + KV cache snapshot, or a compressed/derived representation (e.g., token offsets, model variant id, latency per token)? Full snapshots blow up storage quickly.
2) Retention & privacy: what is the retention window? Will customers be able to opt-in/out? We need this to align with current retention policy and encryption-at-rest flows.
3) Sandbox replay cost: if we support live replays on demand, what's the expected QPS? For small customers it's negligible, for enterprise customers like Acme we should cap replays or meter them.

I sketched an initial ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7824 — proposes a "trace snippet" model first (store derived metadata + pointer to raw logs for 7 days), and a staged replay feature that runs on a dedicated sandbox pool with strict quotas.

If we go with snippet-only for MVP, the infra ask is moderate: small indexed store + UI surface. Full replay needs a sandbox runtime and rejiggered routing logic.

Assigning Dylan/Brian for rough infra estimates would help.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Runtime Engineering
aditya@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 15:30:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: trace-playback for high-cost chat flows

On Thu, May 16, 2028 at 11:05 AM Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Mateo — digging into the ask, a few technical clarifications/questions before we commit scope:
> 
> 1) Data model: do we intend to store the full token stream + KV cache snapshot, or a compressed/derived representation ...

Quick proposal from Observability:
Short-term (MVP, 2 sprints):
- Implement "trace snippet" in Console: show per-request metadata (model id, variant, token counts), a per-token aggregate cost estimate, and a clickable link to raw logs (7d retention). No full KV snapshots.
- UI: add a lightweight playback button that re-executes the request in a *read-only sandbox* that uses a cached model variant; replay runs in a quota-limited dedicated pool.

Medium-term (Q3):
- Full replay with optional KV-state capture for debugging production-only issues. Requires explicit customer opt-in and stronger access controls.
- Rollout: dark-launch snippet for internal CS + 2 pilot customers (Acme + BetaCorp), then gradual console exposure.

Risks / notes: 
- Storage: snippets are small; full snapshots increase S3/DB cost.
- Security: sandbox must never write customer outputs to primary storage. We'll need consent UI and audit logs.

I've attached a short deck with UI mockups and a proposed rollout timeline. Suggest we designate a PM to own the feature and a runtime lead (Aditya) + observability owner (Evelyn) + solutions contact (Mateo).

Attachments: playback-proposal.pdf, trace-snippet-example.png

Evelyn Hart
Director, Observability 
evelyn@redwood.com

From: Sara Kim <sara@acmecorp.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: trace-playback for high-cost chat flows

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear proposal. A couple quick notes from Acme: 
- The sample CSV I attached highlights the three chat templates that drive 75% of our excess cost; being able to replay those end-to-end would let our SREs validate changes before we flip to cheaper variants.
- Retention: we'd be willing to opt into a 30-day opt-in for replayable traces for those three flows only.
- Procurement: adding this feature into our contract would help justify the expansion we discussed. Can we aim for a pilot by the end of June?

Would also welcome a weekly 30-min sync while design/infra are scoped — Mateo, can you set something up?

Best,
Sara Kim
Platform PM, Acme Corp
